original_question: What type of leukemia is associated with the gene mutated in Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines?

final_qi.question: What type of leukemia is associated with the gene mutated in Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines?
final_qi.long_answer: Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines (LEOPARD syndrome) most often involves activating mutations of the PTPN11 gene encoding the SHP-2 tyrosine phosphatase. The same PTPN11 mutations are a major driver in hematologic malignancy, particularly juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML), being present in roughly one-third of JMML cases. Hence, the leukemia classically associated with the gene mutated in this syndrome is juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.
